public_rationale: The evidence supports persistent reasoning errors, hallucinations and safeguard weaknesses in several important 2024 models. Structured Outputs also shows a real improvement relevant to the software-integration prediction, although it does not guarantee correct content. These findings do not establish that the six predictions largely held for every relevant model. They also do not identify a model that clearly defeats the overall pattern.
limitations: Selected benchmarks cannot establish a universal claim.
The original predictions combine several different capabilities and risks.
Improved performance and continued unreliability can both be true.

our_interpretation: Assess the six substantive predictions, excluding the seventh as Marcus expressly does.

The original six concern unpredictable errors; unreliable reasoning and medical advice; hallucinations and imperfect safeguards; unreliable downstream software integration; absence of unaided general intelligence; and unresolved alignment.
Read 'largely' as preservation of that overall pattern, allowing improvements and exceptions within individual predictions. Do not invent a numerical passing score.
Read 'every model' in context as every relevant GPT-like general-purpose model released in 2024. Tests of selected frontier models cannot establish that universal statement by themselves.
The target period is calendar 2024, explicitly named in the claim.
criteria.support_condition: Evaluations covering the relevant 2024 models establish that the overall pattern of the six predictions persisted across them.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A documented 2024 model clearly escapes the overall pattern. An improvement on one benchmark alone does not contradict 'largely'.
